headline: Re-estimated through 2025, Blanchard-Katz's mechanism holds but the out-migration share of a state's year-1 adjustment has fallen from 0.38 (1978-90) to ~0.28 (2011-25) - states now lean less on people leaving.

metrics.label: Year-1 out-migration share (household)
metrics.baseline_label: this study original-sample & paper household benchmark
metrics.note: share of a job loss absorbed by net out-migration; fell ~1/3

metrics.label: Year-1 UR response to -1% emp shock
metrics.note: still peaks then dies out; half-life 3-4 yrs in every window

metrics.label: Growth-persistence slope (Fig-1)
metrics.note: cross-generation growth ranks much less sticky now

tables.title: C3 adjustment evolution (household emp, 90% state-cluster bootstrap)

figures.caption: C3 flagship: year-1 UR response, UR half-life, year-10 employment response, and implied year-1 out-migration share, in 15-yr rolling windows 1978-2025. Blue = household-employment baseline with 90% state-cluster bootstrap bands; star = BK 1992 (1978-90); dashed = paper's printed value; orange = COVID-dummied overlay.
figures.alt: Four line panels versus window-end year; migration share (panel d) drifts down from ~0.38 toward ~0.25, below the 0.40 reference line.

figures.caption: Supporting: C1 growth persistence (Fig-1 slopes fade 0.71->0.37) and shock permanence (AR(4) IR stays ~1.5-2.0); C2 unemployment IR (year-10 ~0 throughout); C4 income trough and the convergence stall; and the household-vs-payroll migration split.
figures.alt: Six panels of rolling-window estimates, each with the original BK value marked, showing which facts held and which faded.

notes: C3 baseline uses household (LAUS) survey employment, benchmark migration 0.40 (paper fn 37); payroll/establishment shown as 1990+ robustness (benchmark 0.65, ~0.63 recently).
No SIC->NAICS splice needed: FRED {ST}NAN state nonfarm series is continuous 1939-2025 (splice_ratios.csv ratio=1.0).
C2 year-5 IR gate lands at 0.08 vs paper 0.29 - reproduces the replication's 0.08; a LAUS-only (post-1976) short-window feature, not a bug. Year-10 ~0 confirms mean-reversion.

Direction of change matches Dao-Furceri-Loungani (2017) (migration's role falling) and Ganong-Shoag (convergence stall); original values cited from /workspace/eval/replication/codebase/results/*.json.
